subject.title: Feature: groupScope option to consolidate group sessions into main

question: Should OpenClaw permit selected group or channel bindings to enter the private main session, and if so should that be limited to exact per-binding opt-ins rather than also allowing a global groupScope default?
rationale: This changes which people and untrusted messages share the main transcript, memory context, queue, and tool-bearing session; source correctness alone cannot choose the intended privacy and product boundary.

options.title: Exact binding opt-in
options.body: Allow only explicitly matched group or channel bindings to use main, preserving isolation everywhere else and documenting the trust consequence.

options.title: Global plus binding overrides
options.body: Accept the linked PR's broader global default and override model, with explicit warnings and comprehensive fresh-install and upgrade proof.

options.title: Named shared sessions only
options.body: Defer main-session folding and implement the broader named shared-session model tracked at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/19929.

recommendation.title: Exact binding opt-in
recommendation.body: Allow only explicitly matched group or channel bindings to use main, preserving isolation everywhere else and documenting the trust consequence.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing-history and repository product-direction owner for deciding whether main-session sharing is an acceptable trust boundary.
